channelTitle: Forget the medicine cabinet, Grandma June reaches for this flower first
hook: Forget the medicine cabinet, for a small scrape Grandma June reaches for this flower first.
remedy: As a classic piece of old-fashioned home wisdom, calendula flowers infused into oil and made into a simple salve were kept on hand and dabbed onto minor cuts and scrapes as a soothing, old-fashioned skin care staple.
steps: Infuse dried calendula petals in a neutral oil for a few weeks, or use a store-bought calendula oil
Warm the oil gently and melt in a little beeswax to thicken it into a salve
Let it set in a small jar, then dab a little onto clean, minor cuts and scrapes
caution: Not for deep wounds, animal bites, or anything showing signs of infection. Those allergic to ragweed or daisies should patch-test first.
cta: Do you keep a calendula salve on hand, or is this your first time hearing about it? Tell Grandma June in the comments.
